'''Lara Alcock''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|NTF}} is a British [[mathematics education|mathematics educator]]. She is a professor in mathematics education at [[Loughborough University]], head of the Mathematics Education Centre at Loughborough, and the author of several books on mathematics.<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref><ref name=mec/>
Alcock won the Selden Prize for her research in mathematics education{{r|selden}} and the inaugural [[John Blake University Teaching Medal]] in 2021.<ref name="johnblakemedal"/> Alcock is a [[National Teaching Fellowship|National Teaching Fellow]].<ref name=the/>

==Education ==
Alcock earned bachelor's and master's degrees in mathematics at the [[University of Warwick]], and in 2001 completed a [[PhD]] in mathematics education at Warwick.{{r|mec|selden}} Her PhD research on ''Categories, definitions and mathematics: Student reasoning about objects in analysis'', was supervised by Adrian Simpson.<ref name=phd>{{cite thesis|title=Categories, definitions and mathematics : student reasoning about objects in analysis|first=Lara|last=Alcock|year=2001|publisher=University of Warwick|url=https://wrap.warwick.ac.uk/56117/|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.246820}}|oclc=921054748|degree=PhD}}</ref> 

==Career and research==
After working as an assistant professor at [[Rutgers University]] in New Jersey, she returned to the UK as a [[teaching fellow]] at [[Essex University]]. She moved to Loughborough in 2007.<ref name=mec>{{citation|url=http://www.lboro.ac.uk/departments/mec/staff/lara-alcock.html|title=Centre Staff: Dr Lara Alcock|publisher=Loughborough University Mathematics Education Centre|accessdate=2018-09-12|archive-date=2018-09-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180913040227/http://www.lboro.ac.uk/departments/mec/staff/lara-alcock.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=mr>Reviews of ''Mathematics Rebooted'': {{citation|title=Review|date=February 2018|publisher=European Mathematical Society|url=http://euro-math-soc.eu/review/mathematics-rebooted|first=Adhemar|last=Bultheel|authorlink=Adhemar Bultheel|access-date=2018-09-12|archive-date=2023-01-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230129032215/https://euro-math-soc.eu/review/mathematics-rebooted|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Review|journal=MAA Reviews|first=Allen|last=Stenger|date=April 2018|url=https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/mathematics-rebooted-a-fresh-approach-to-understanding|access-date=2018-09-12|archive-date=2023-03-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331154137/https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/mathematics-rebooted-a-fresh-approach-to-understanding|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Review|journal=Newsletter of the London Mathematical Society|volume=480|date=January 2019|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/sites/lms.ac.uk/files/files/NLMS_480.pdf|pages=39–40|first=Michael|last=Grove}}
</ref><ref name=selden>{{citation|url=https://www.maa.org/2012-selden-prize-winner|title=2012 Selden Prize Winner|publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]]|accessdate=2018-09-12|archive-date=2015-09-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150909171617/http://www.maa.org/2012-selden-prize-winner|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Publications===
Alcock's publications<ref name=gs/> include:
* ''Ideas from Mathematics Education: An Introduction for Mathematicians'' (with Adrian Simpson, Higher Education Academy, 2009)
* ''How to Study for a Mathematics Degree'' / ''How to Study as a Mathematics Major'' (UK/US; Oxford University Press, 2013); ''Wie man erfolgreich Mathematik studiert'' (translated into German by Bernhard Gerl, Springer Spektrum, 2017)<ref name=hs>{{citation | last = Foster | first = Colin | date = July 2014 | doi = 10.1017/s0025557200001625| issue = 542 | journal = The Mathematical Gazette | pages = 377–378 | title = none | volume = 98}}</ref><ref>{{citation | last = Storr | first = Graham |date = 2014 | doi = 10.1017/s0025557200008457 | issue = 543 | journal = The Mathematical Gazette | page = 547 | title = none | volume = 98| s2cid = 184177892 | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Review|first=Annie|last=Selden|authorlink=Annie Selden|journal=MAA Reviews|date=September 2013|url=https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/how-to-study-as-a-mathematics-major|access-date=2018-09-12|archive-date=2018-09-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180913040331/https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/how-to-study-as-a-mathematics-major|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{citation | last = Panse | first = Anja | date = 2018 | doi = 10.1007/s00591-018-0219-6 | issue = 1 | journal = Mathematische Semesterberichte | pages = 133–135 | title = none | volume = 65| s2cid = 125487245 }}</ref>
* ''How to Think about Analysis'' (Oxford University Press, 2014)<ref name=ta>{{citation|title=Review of How to Think about Analysis|first=Stanley R.|last=Huddy|date=January 2015|journal=MAA Reviews|url=https://old.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/how-to-think-about-analysis}}</ref>
* ''Mathematics Rebooted: A Fresh Approach to Understanding'' (Oxford University Press, 2017)<ref name=mr/>
* ''How to Think About Abstract Algebra'' (Oxford University Press, 2021)<ref name="absalg">{{cite web |title=How to Think About Abstract Algebra |url=https://global.oup.com/ukhe/product/how-to-think-about-abstract-algebra-9780198843382?cc=se&lang=en& |publisher=Oxford University Press |access-date=19 February 2025}}</ref>

===Awards and honours===
Alcock is the 2012 winner of the Annie and John Selden Prize for research in undergraduate [[mathematics education]], given by the [[Mathematical Association of America]].<ref name=selden/> She was named a National Teaching Fellow by the [[Higher Education Academy]] in 2015.<ref name=the>{{citation|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/national-teaching-fellows-2015-named|newspaper=[[Times Higher Education]]|title=National Teaching Fellows of 2015 are named: Fifty-five people working in universities have been named as the latest winners of the sector's top honour for teaching and learning|first=Jack|last=Grove|date=11 June 2015}}</ref>

Alcock was the inaugural winner of the [[Institute of Mathematics and its Applications]] John Blake University Teaching Medal in 2021. <ref name="johnblakemedal">{{cite web |title=Dr Lara Alcock wins the inaugural IMA John Blake University Teaching Medal |date=16 July 2021 |url=https://ima.org.uk/17381/dr-lara-alcock-wins-the-inaugural-ima-john-blake-university-teaching-medal/ |publisher=Institute of Mathematics & its Applications |access-date=8 August 2021}}</ref>
